She said that she would dance with me if I brought her red roses, cried the young Student. <break time="0.8s" /> But in all my garden there is no red rose. <break time="0.8s" /> He lay on the grass and cried, and his beautiful eyes filled with tears. <break time="0.8s" /> Because I have no red rose, my life is sad and empty. <break time="0.8s" /> From her nest in the oak tree, the Nightingale heard him and wondered. <break time="0.8s" /> She was a small brown bird who sang every night in the garden. <break time="0.8s" /> Here at last is a true lover, said the Nightingale. <break time="0.8s" /> Night after night I have sung of him, though I did not know him. <break time="0.8s" /> Now I see him, and his face is as pale as ivory. <break time="0.8s" /> The Student said that the Prince was giving a ball the next night, and his love would be there. <break time="0.8s" /> If I bring her a red rose, she will dance with me until dawn.

그녀는 나와 춤을 추겠다고 말했어. <break time="0.8s" /> 내가 붉은 장미를 가져오면. <break time="0.8s" /> 젊은 대학생이 울부짖었다. <break time="0.8s" /> 하지만 내 정원 어디에도. <break time="0.8s" /> 붉은 장미가 없어. <break time="0.8s" /> 그는 풀밭에 누웠다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그리고 울었다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그리고 그의 아름다운 눈은. <break time="0.8s" /> 눈물로 가득 찼다. <break time="0.8s" /> 붉은 장미가 없어서. <break time="0.8s" /> 내 삶은 슬프고 텅 비었어. <break time="0.8s" /> 자기 둥지에서. <break time="0.8s" /> 떡갈나무에 있는. <break time="0.8s" /> 나이팅게일이 그의 말을 들었다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그리고 궁금해했다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그녀는 작은 갈색 새였다. <break time="0.8s" /> 매일 밤 정원에서 노래하는. <break time="0.8s" /> 드디어 여기 진정한 연인이 있구나. <break time="0.8s" /> 나이팅게일이 말했다. <break time="0.8s" /> 밤마다 나는 그에 대해 노래해 왔어. <break time="0.8s" /> 그를 알지 못했지만. <break time="0.8s" /> 이제 그를 보니. <break time="0.8s" /> 그의 얼굴이 상아처럼 창백하구나. <break time="0.8s" /> 대학생은 말했다 왕자가 무도회를 연다고. <break time="0.8s" /> 다음 날 밤에. <break time="0.8s" /> 그리고 사랑하는 그녀도 그곳에 올 거라고. <break time="0.8s" /> 그녀에게 붉은 장미를 가져가면. <break time="0.8s" /> 그녀는 나와 춤을 출 거야. <break time="0.8s" /> 새벽까지.

A little green lizard. <break time="0.8s" /> A butterfly, and a daisy. <break time="0.8s" /> Asked why he was weeping. <break time="0.8s" /> He is weeping for a red rose. <break time="0.8s" /> Said the Nightingale. <break time="0.8s" /> For a red rose. <break time="0.8s" /> How very silly. <break time="0.8s" /> They cried. <break time="0.8s" /> And the lizard laughed out loud. <break time="0.8s" /> But the Nightingale understood his sorrow. <break time="0.8s" /> And she sat silently. <break time="0.8s" /> In the oak tree. <break time="0.8s" /> Suddenly she spread her brown wings. <break time="0.8s" /> And flew to a rose tree. <break time="0.8s" /> In the middle of the grass. <break time="0.8s" /> Give me a red rose. <break time="0.8s" /> And I will sing you my sweetest song. <break time="0.8s" /> She cried. <break time="0.8s" /> But the tree shook its head. <break time="0.8s" /> And said, My roses are white. <break time="0.8s" /> The yellow rose tree. <break time="0.8s" /> That grew by the old sundial. <break time="0.8s" /> Also shook its head. <break time="0.8s" /> At last she found the rose tree. <break time="0.8s" /> Which grew beneath the Students window. <break time="0.8s" /> My roses are red. <break time="0.8s" /> It said. <break time="0.8s" /> But the winter has chilled my veins. <break time="0.8s" /> And the storm has broken my branches. <break time="0.8s" /> There is a way. <break time="0.8s" /> But it is so terrible. <break time="0.8s" /> That I am afraid to tell you.

A little green lizard, a butterfly, and a daisy asked why he was weeping. <break time="0.8s" /> He is weeping for a red rose, said the Nightingale. <break time="0.8s" /> For a red rose, How very silly, they cried, and the lizard laughed out loud. <break time="0.8s" /> But the Nightingale understood his sorrow, and she sat silently in the oak tree. <break time="0.8s" /> Suddenly she spread her brown wings and flew to a rose tree in the middle of the grass. <break time="0.8s" /> Give me a red rose, and I will sing you my sweetest song, she cried. <break time="0.8s" /> But the tree shook its head and said, My roses are white. <break time="0.8s" /> The yellow rose tree that grew by the old sundial also shook its head. <break time="0.8s" /> At last she found the rose tree which grew beneath the Students window. <break time="0.8s" /> My roses are red, it said, but the winter has chilled my veins, and the storm has broken my branches. <break time="0.8s" /> There is a way, but it is so terrible that I am afraid to tell you.

작은 초록 도마뱀과. <break time="0.8s" /> 나비와 데이지꽃이. <break time="0.8s" /> 그가 왜 울고 있는지 물었다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그는 붉은 장미 때문에 울고 있어. <break time="0.8s" /> 나이팅게일이 말했다. <break time="0.8s" /> 붉은 장미 때문에. <break time="0.8s" /> 정말 바보 같아. <break time="0.8s" /> 그들이 외쳤다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그리고 도마뱀은 소리 내어 웃었다. <break time="0.8s" /> 하지만 나이팅게일은 그의 슬픔을 이해했다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그리고 그녀는 조용히 앉아 있었다. <break time="0.8s" /> 떡갈나무에. <break time="0.8s" /> 갑자기 그녀는 갈색 날개를 폈다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그리고 장미나무로 날아갔다. <break time="0.8s" /> 풀밭 한가운데 있는. <break time="0.8s" /> 붉은 장미를 한 송이 줘. <break time="0.8s" /> 그러면 내 가장 달콤한 노래를 불러 줄게. <break time="0.8s" /> 그녀가 외쳤다. <break time="0.8s" /> 하지만 나무는 고개를 저었다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그리고 말했다 내 장미는 하얀색이야. <break time="0.8s" /> 노란 장미나무도. <break time="0.8s" /> 오래된 해시계 옆에서 자라는. <break time="0.8s" /> 고개를 저었다. <break time="0.8s" /> 마침내 그녀는 장미나무를 찾았다. <break time="0.8s" /> 대학생의 창문 아래에서 자라는. <break time="0.8s" /> 내 장미는 붉은색이야. <break time="0.8s" /> 나무가 말했다. <break time="0.8s" /> 하지만 겨울이 내 속을 얼어붙게 했어. <break time="0.8s" /> 그리고 폭풍이 내 가지를 부러뜨렸어. <break time="0.8s" /> 방법이 하나 있어. <break time="0.8s" /> 하지만 그것은 너무 끔찍해서. <break time="0.8s" /> 너에게 말하기가 두려워.

Tell me the way. <break time="0.8s" /> Said the Nightingale. <break time="0.8s" /> For I am not afraid. <break time="0.8s" /> You must make the rose. <break time="0.8s" /> Out of music by moonlight. <break time="0.8s" /> Said the tree. <break time="0.8s" /> All night long. <break time="0.8s" /> You must sing. <break time="0.8s" /> With your breast against a thorn. <break time="0.8s" /> The thorn will pierce your heart. <break time="0.8s" /> And your life will flow. <break time="0.8s" /> Into my veins. <break time="0.8s" /> Death is a great price. <break time="0.8s" /> To pay for a red rose. <break time="0.8s" /> Cried the Nightingale. <break time="0.8s" /> And Life is very dear to all. <break time="0.8s" /> Yet Love is better than Life. <break time="0.8s" /> And what is the heart of a bird. <break time="0.8s" /> Compared to the heart of a man. <break time="0.8s" /> She flew back to the Student. <break time="0.8s" /> And said, Be happy. <break time="0.8s" /> For you shall have your red rose. <break time="0.8s" /> All that I ask. <break time="0.8s" /> Is that you will be a true lover. <break time="0.8s" /> The Student looked up and listened. <break time="0.8s" /> But he could not understand her. <break time="0.8s" /> Because he only knew. <break time="0.8s" /> The things that are written in books. <break time="0.8s" /> But the oak tree. <break time="0.8s" /> Who loved the little Nightingale. <break time="0.8s" /> Felt sad. <break time="0.8s" /> And asked her for one last song. <break time="0.8s" /> When she finished her song. <break time="0.8s" /> The Student said. <break time="0.8s" /> She sings beautifully. <break time="0.8s" /> But she has no real feeling. <break time="0.8s" /> She would never give up anything. <break time="0.8s" /> For others. <break time="0.8s" /> He thought.

Tell me the way, said the Nightingale, for I am not afraid. <break time="0.8s" /> You must make the rose out of music by moonlight, said the tree. <break time="0.8s" /> All night long you must sing with your breast against a thorn. <break time="0.8s" /> The thorn will pierce your heart, and your life will flow into my veins. <break time="0.8s" /> Death is a great price to pay for a red rose, cried the Nightingale, and Life is very dear to all. <break time="0.8s" /> Yet Love is better than Life, and what is the heart of a bird compared to the heart of a man. <break time="0.8s" /> She flew back to the Student and said, Be happy, for you shall have your red rose. <break time="0.8s" /> All that I ask is that you will be a true lover. <break time="0.8s" /> The Student looked up and listened, but he could not understand her, because he only knew the things that are written in books. <break time="0.8s" /> But the oak tree, who loved the little Nightingale, felt sad and asked her for one last song. <break time="0.8s" /> When she finished her song, the Student said, She sings beautifully, but she has no real feeling. <break time="0.8s" /> She would never give up anything for others, he thought.

그 방법을 말해 줘. <break time="0.8s" /> 나이팅게일이 말했다. <break time="0.8s" /> 나는 두렵지 않으니까. <break time="0.8s" /> 너는 장미를 만들어야 해. <break time="0.8s" /> 달빛 아래에서 음악으로. <break time="0.8s" /> 나무가 말했다. <break time="0.8s" /> 밤새도록. <break time="0.8s" /> 너는 노래해야 해. <break time="0.8s" /> 가슴을 가시에 댄 채로. <break time="0.8s" /> 가시가 네 심장을 찌를 거야. <break time="0.8s" /> 그리고 네 생명이 흘러들 거야. <break time="0.8s" /> 내 속으로. <break time="0.8s" /> 죽음은 큰 값이야. <break time="0.8s" /> 붉은 장미 한 송이를 위해 치르기에는. <break time="0.8s" /> 나이팅게일이 외쳤다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그리고 생명은 모두에게 아주 소중해. <break time="0.8s" /> 그래도 사랑은 생명보다 더 좋아. <break time="0.8s" /> 그리고 새의 마음이 무엇이겠어. <break time="0.8s" /> 사람의 마음에 비하면. <break time="0.8s" /> 그녀는 대학생에게 다시 날아갔다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그리고 말했다 기뻐해. <break time="0.8s" /> 너는 붉은 장미를 갖게 될 테니까. <break time="0.8s" /> 내가 바라는 모든 것은. <break time="0.8s" /> 네가 진정한 연인이 되는 것이야. <break time="0.8s" /> 대학생은 고개를 들고 귀를 기울였다. <break time="0.8s" /> 하지만 그녀의 말을 이해하지 못했다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그가 아는 것이라곤. <break time="0.8s" /> 책에 쓰여 있는 것들뿐이었기 때문이다. <break time="0.8s" /> 하지만 떡갈나무는. <break time="0.8s" /> 작은 나이팅게일을 사랑했는데. <break time="0.8s" /> 슬퍼졌다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그리고 그녀에게 마지막 노래를 한 곡 청했다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그녀가 노래를 마치자. <break time="0.8s" /> 대학생이 말했다. <break time="0.8s" /> 그녀는 노래를 아름답게 부르지만. <break time="0.8s" /> 진짜 감정은 없어. <break time="0.8s" /> 그녀는 절대 아무것도 내주지 않을 거야. <break time="0.8s" /> 남을 위해서는. <break time="0.8s" /> 그는 생각했다.

That night. <break time="0.8s" /> The Student went to bed. <break time="0.8s" /> And fell asleep. <break time="0.8s" /> Thinking of his love. <break time="0.8s" /> When the moon shone in the sky. <break time="0.8s" /> The Nightingale flew to the rose tree. <break time="0.8s" /> And pressed her breast. <break time="0.8s" /> Against the thorn. <break time="0.8s" /> All night long she sang. <break time="0.8s" /> And the cold white moon. <break time="0.8s" /> Leaned down and listened. <break time="0.8s" /> She sang first of the love. <break time="0.8s" /> That is born in the heart of a boy and a girl. <break time="0.8s" /> On the top of the tree. <break time="0.8s" /> A lovely rose began to bloom. <break time="0.8s" /> But it was pale. <break time="0.8s" /> Like the mist over the river. <break time="0.8s" /> Press closer, little Nightingale. <break time="0.8s" /> Cried the tree. <break time="0.8s" /> Or the day will come. <break time="0.8s" /> Before the rose is finished. <break time="0.8s" /> So she pressed closer. <break time="0.8s" /> And her song grew louder and louder. <break time="0.8s" /> A soft pink came. <break time="0.8s" /> Into the leaves of the rose. <break time="0.8s" /> But its heart was still white. <break time="0.8s" /> At last the thorn touched her heart. <break time="0.8s" /> And she felt a sharp pain. <break time="0.8s" /> She sang of the love. <break time="0.8s" /> That never dies. <break time="0.8s" /> And the rose became deep red. <break time="0.8s" /> Like the morning sky. <break time="0.8s" /> Then her voice grew weak. <break time="0.8s" /> And her little wings. <break time="0.8s" /> Began to beat. <break time="0.8s" /> Look, the rose is finished. <break time="0.8s" /> Cried the tree. <break time="0.8s" /> But the Nightingale lay dead. <break time="0.8s" /> In the long grass.
